_readme: Location-gate corpus: every distinct `location` string in the operator's live DB (db/applications.db, captured 2026-07-30; 9,633 rows with a location / 1,611 distinct). COMMITTED, unlike apps/worker/eval/ -- a board location string is a place name, not JD text or resume context, so the privacy rule that keeps the other golden sets out of git does not apply, and committing it is what lets CI gate the invariant. LABELS COME FROM AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE, never from resolve_location -- a corpus labeled by the code under test only asserts that the code agrees with itself. The oracle is a deliberately dumb substring scan sharing no code with score/location.py: `us` is true when the string names the US or a US state in full; `foreign` lists ISO codes for full country names (>=4 chars, so no 2-letter codes, and no English-word collisions like Jersey/Georgia/Turkey). expect=keep when US and nothing foreign; expect=discard when foreign and nothing US; expect=either when the oracle ABSTAINS (mixed signals, or a city-only string it cannot judge) -- those rows are reported, never gated. THE GATE IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL: zero false discards, no tolerance. A leak costs one paid fit call and still reaches the human; a false discard deletes a real job that nobody reviews. Leaks are therefore PINNED, not zero. REBUILD: SELECT location, COUNT(*) FROM job_postings WHERE location IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(location) <> '' GROUP BY 1.
